props.title: The Last Mogul
props.initialSlug: One man's empire, one man's fall.

sections.content: **The Last Mogul (2005)** (2005) offers a razor-sharp look at Hollywood power broker Lew Wasserman, who transformed the entertainment industry more than any mogul since the studio system's founders. Director Barry Avrich digs deep into how Wasserman revolutionized talent agencies with MCA, broke studio control over actors through percentage deals, and essentially created the modern blockbuster system. This documentary pairs perfectly with **Citizen Kane** (1941) in showing how media titans shaped 20th century entertainment, while films like **The Player** (1992) and **The Bad and the Beautiful** (1952) dramatize the ruthless deal-making Wasserman mastered.

sections.content: Wasserman's influence extends through modern Hollywood, visible in works like **Entourage** (2015) and **Trumbo** (2015). His pioneering of package deals - bundling talent, scripts, and directors - created the template for modern agencies like CAA. The documentary reveals how he navigated the transition from classic Hollywood to New Hollywood, working with everyone from Alfred Hitchcock to Steven Spielberg. His fingerprints are all over films about industry power plays like **Swimming with Sharks** (1994) and **What Just Happened** (2008). SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Hollywood Power Structures

The film industry's power dynamics that Wasserman helped establish are reflected in movies like **The Big Picture** (1989) and **Get Shorty** (1995). His impact on television - particularly through Universal Studios - set up the modern entertainment landscape explored in **Network** (1976) and **Quiz Show** (1994). Wasserman's ability to adapt from the studio system through the corporate era makes **The Last Mogul** essential viewing for understanding how Hollywood really works.
